key_insight: Withholding poorly supported or high-disagreement patient simulations improves factual prediction reliability at the cost of coverage.
engineering_relevance: Support and ensemble-disagreement gates offer a lightweight reliability layer for simulation-driven clinical agents, with abstention when no candidate qualifies.
method: Predict short-horizon physiological responses to norepinephrine dose categories using a recurrent dynamics ensemble.
Estimate observational action support with a behavior model and withhold simulations that fail support or disagreement thresholds.
Integrate gating into a propose–simulate–refine agent that abstains when all candidates are rejected.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used 30,700 eICU-CRD transitions across 70 hospitals, with 14 held out; at 62.0% factual-transition coverage, joint gating achieved 7.3 mmHg MAP MAE versus 9.2 mmHg for random selection at matched coverage.
watch_item: Factual prediction accuracy and agreement with recorded actions do not establish individualized treatment effects or improved patient outcomes.
paper_title: When to Trust Simulated Patient Responses:Support-Gated World Models for Vasopressor Decision Support
